prompt:
Vertical 9:16 editorial wedding-night photograph at high resolution, a full-bleed photograph edge to edge with no borders, bands or panels; 100 mm macro-portrait lens at ear height. The camera is behind a young Indian woman at a sangeet under a shamiana, a little to her left, about 20 cm from her left ear. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy its construction exactly and ignore its background and light. Reference 2 is a detail of the same piece. Ignore the plaster block in both; reference 2 shows the open braid and its see-through core up close.
NO FACE: her head is turned fully away from the camera, so the jaw and cheek are hidden behind the ear and hair; no eyelash, eyelid, brow, cheek, nose or lip breaks the outline of her head anywhere in the frame (on the first take her head was only three-quarters away and eyelashes and a brow tail showed past the cheek; never again).
FIDELITY: one hoop worn on her left earlobe: a round hoop 25 mm across, a 5-6 mm open plait of polished round wires laid in pairs, braided in chevrons over a see-through core of finer wires; one flat 8 mm disc at the top on the latch side; one thin hinged latch wire; no stones; no bottom loop; 18k gold tone, mirror polish. It must stay a many-wire open braid, never a smooth tube, a simple twist or an oval; do not redesign or add anything.
THE BRAID, copied exactly from reference 2: a chunky, rounded, three-dimensional open plait about 5-6 mm thick, as deep as it is wide; made of many separate, individually rounded, mirror-polished wires laid in pairs, each pair crossing over and under the next in chevrons; between the outer wires you can see straight through to an inner core of finer wires and to the skin behind; every wire carries its own bright highlight. It is NOT a flat three-strand ribbon braid, NOT bundles of parallel grooved or brushed wires, NOT engraved lines, NOT a smooth tube, NOT a twisted rope (twice before it came out as a flat three-strand ribbon of grouped, parallel, grooved wires; that is wrong).
THE DISC: exactly ONE flat, round, mirror-polished disc, about one third of the hoop's width, on the latch end only, where the hoop meets the earlobe on the side away from the hinge; the other end is a small cylindrical hinge knuckle with NO disc. Never two discs (the first take invented a second disc on the hinge end).
THE LATCH: one thin curved latch wire swings from the hinge knuckle, passes through the earlobe piercing and clicks into the catch behind the disc, so the hoop is one closed ring hanging from the lobe; no gap in the ring, no loose stubs, no small loops or jump rings.
METAL: every wire, the disc, the hinge knuckle and the latch wire are the same mirror-polished warm-neutral 18k gold tone; never satin, brushed, matte, brassy, orange or two-tone.
SCALE, true size: field of view about 11 cm wide, so the whole ear fits in the frame with room around it. Scale by the ear: the hoop's outer width is a little less than half the ear's height from the top of the ear to the tip of the lobe; two hoops stacked would not reach the top of the ear; the hoop is about the size of a 25 mm coin (twice before it was drawn at 0.59-0.62 of the ear's height, about 1.4 times too big; never again). The latch wire runs through the lobe and the lower curve of the hoop rests against the side of her neck with a soft, true contact shadow on the skin.
BODY AND PLACEMENT: her left ear sits on the left outline of her head, a little right of the frame's centre; the hoop's centre is about 60% of the way across the frame from the left and just above the middle of the frame's height, the disc at about 37% of the height and the bottom of the hoop no lower than 50%. Beyond the outline of her head, the left part of the frame is only out-of-focus plum night, never a cheek. The back of her head, smooth black hair and a low bun fill the right side; bare nape with fine downy hair; the lower half of the frame is the long side of her neck going down into an ivory raw-silk blouse collar and plum shadow.
CLEAN SPACE ROUND THE HOOP: keep a calm, evenly lit area about 5 cm across centred on the hoop, the hoop sharp and fully visible: inside that area only the hoop, the lobe, the skin and hair it touches and soft dark bokeh; no fingers, glasses, temple arms, loose hairs or bright bokeh cross it, and nothing is in front of the hoop.
THE AUNTY: from the left edge, an older Indian woman's hand, about sixty, warm brown skin with soft creases, short bare nails, no rings, bangles, watch or mehendi, the wrist under a rani-pink silk pallu, holds her folded reading glasses beside the hoop, never in front of it: dark tortoiseshell half-moon reading glasses, flat-topped D-shaped lenses with the straight edge on top and the curve below, thin dark tortoiseshell rims, a thin bridge, both temple arms folded; she pinches one folded temple arm between thumb and fingers. The near lens hangs at the height of the hoop over the dark background to the left of the ear, its nearest edge about 2 cm left of the clean area; the bridge and the other lens may run off the left edge. Never round, oval, cat-eye or full-height lenses (the first take had a round full-rim frame). The glass is perfectly clear and untinted, with no reflection streak; through it only out-of-focus plum bokeh, never the hoop, never a face or eyes.
WORLD: a plum-dark shamiana at night with soft marigold fairy-light bokeh, all soft round points.
COMPOSITION: from 14% to 32% of the frame's height, on the left and centre, only calm out-of-focus plum bokeh with soft marigold points, no hand and no glasses, kept clear for the headline; the hoop, the lobe and the glasses between 33% and 53%; the aunty's wrist and pink pallu only at the left edge; below 55% only the side of her neck, soft ivory silk and plum shadow, darker toward the bottom, calm and clear for the price card.
LIGHT: two lights only: a soft warm fill from the fairy lights above left, and one small hard specular kicker from behind right that puts a crisp highlight on every polished wire of the braid and on the disc; the hoop is evenly lit with no shadow across it. Warm-neutral 18k gold tone, never brassy or orange.
NEGATIVES: no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark anywhere; no face, no eyes, no eyelashes, no eyebrows anywhere, never reflected in the glasses; one product only: no second earring, no necklace, no nose pin; no second disc, no jump rings, no gap in the hoop; no magnifier and no magnified view anywhere; no round or full-rim glasses; no rings or bangles on anyone; no star-shaped glints.

Vertical 9:16 editorial late-night photograph at high resolution, a full-bleed photograph edge to edge with no borders, bands or panels; 100 mm macro lens, a close view from slightly above of a young Indian woman's right hand at a wedding's catering-tent chai counter at 1 a.m., while an aunty, her glasses in hand, leans in to look. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy its construction exactly and ignore its background and light. Reference 2 is a detail of the same piece. Reference 2 shows the ring worn on one finger, close up, at true scale: copy how the two stones sit on the finger, never its framing. Ignore the plaster cube in reference 1.
FIDELITY: the ring on her index finger, the topmost finger curled round the glass, stones on top (the first take put it on the middle finger): an open bypass ring of one smooth round 1.5 mm wire in 18k gold tone, about 17 mm inside, whose two ends pass side by side; each end holds one cushion stone in one slim plain polished bezel, set diagonally, corners nearly touching: one opaque banded golden-brown tiger eye about 11.8 mm with a softly faceted top, and one transparent faceted pale champagne crystal of about the same face. No small stones, no prongs, no border of small stones round either stone, high polish. The tiger eye must stay opaque, banded and golden-brown and unmatched beside the clear crystal, never transparent, glassy or a twin of the crystal; do not redesign or add anything.
STONES: set diagonally exactly as in reference 2: the tiger eye higher and nearer the knuckle, the crystal lower and nearer the fingertip, offset by most of a stone's height so only one corner of each nearly touches (the first take set them almost side by side). The tiger eye's top shows a few soft irregular facet lines as in both references, never a regular checkerboard (the first take was a checkerboard grid), and stays as deep and dark golden-brown as in the references, not light honey; the crystal pale champagne, faintly warm, never pink or blue.
METAL: the wire and both bezels are one mirror-polished band of warm-neutral 18k gold tone, never orange, copper, brassy or two-tone.
SCALE, true size: field of view about 11 cm wide, so the two stones together span about 20% of the frame's width (the first take was shot about 16 cm wide); the two stones together span about the width of the finger they sit on; her fingers curl round a small ribbed cutting-chai glass 7 cm tall, about three and a half times the ring's width, half full of milky brown tea. The band touches the skin of the finger with a crisp, true contact shadow under it.
HAND: warm wheatish skin, natural texture, five fingers, correct anatomy, short bare nails, no other ring, no bangle, no watch; the back of her hand toward the camera, her wrist leaving the frame at the lower left in shadow.
PLACEMENT: the ring's centre at about 43% of the frame's height and about 42% of its width, a little above the middle of the frame; the chai glass's rim at about 34% of the height, its lower half falling into shadow.
CLEAN SPACE ROUND THE RING: keep a calm, evenly lit area about 5 cm across centred on the ring, the ring sharp and fully visible: inside that area only the ring, the fingers it sits on, the chai glass and dark calm steel; no other hand, no glasses, no temple arm and no bright highlight cross it, and nothing is in front of the ring.
THE AUNTY: from the right edge, at the height of the ring, an older Indian woman's hand, about sixty, warm brown skin with soft creases, short bare nails, no rings, bangles, watch or mehendi, the wrist under a rani-pink silk pallu, holds her folded reading glasses beside the ring, never in front of it or over it: half-moon reading glasses, flat-topped D-shaped lenses with the straight edge on top and the curve below, about 2.5 cm tall, thin dark tortoiseshell rims, a narrow bridge, both temple arms folded; she pinches one folded temple arm between thumb and fingers. The glasses sit to the right of the ring, their nearest edge about 2 cm right of the clean area, and may run off the right edge. Never round, oval or full-height lenses (the first take had round full-rim frames). The glass is perfectly clear and untinted, with no reflection; through it only the out-of-focus counter and night, never the ring or a finger. The ring appears exactly once in the whole picture: no second, smaller or larger copy of the ring or the finger anywhere, inside or outside the glasses (the first take painted a tiny wrong ring on a ghost finger inside the lens; never again); never a face or eyes in the glass.
WORLD: a brushed steel counter top, one bare amber bulb out of frame above, a dented brass kettle small and blurred at the far left between 30% and 45% of the height, dark plum-brown night beyond.
COMPOSITION, on the frame's height: from 0 to 32% only dark plum-brown night with two or three soft amber bokeh points: no kettle, no hand, no pallu and no glasses there, kept clear for the headline; the ring, the hand and the glasses between 33% and 55%, the aunty's hand and the rani-pink pallu only at the right edge; below 60% everything dark and calm (shadowed steel, the base of the glass, the lower fingers), nothing bright, kept clear for the price card.
LIGHT: two lights only: a soft warm amber fill from the bare bulb above left, kept off the metal's key, and one small hard neutral specular kicker from behind right that gives each bezel a bright edge, the tiger eye a silky band of light and the crystal one white catchlight; the 18k gold tone stays warm-neutral, never orange.
NEGATIVES: no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark anywhere; no faces, no eyes, no eyebrows, no reflections of faces; one product only, the ring shown once, no other jewellery on anyone; no magnifier and no magnified or miniature view anywhere; no steam over the ring; no spilled tea.

Vertical 9:16 editorial wedding-night portrait crop at high resolution, a full-bleed photograph edge to edge with no borders, bands or panels; 85 mm lens at collarbone height, front-on: the lower neck, the collarbones and the blouse neckline of an Indian woman of about sixty at a sangeet. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy its construction exactly and ignore its background and light. Reference 2 is a detail of the same piece. Ignore the plaster cube in reference 1; reference 2 shows the clasp worn on skin: copy the clasp's construction exactly from it.
FRAMING AND NO FACE: framed from the base of the neck down to the neckline of her blouse; the top edge of the picture crosses the lower neck about two finger-widths above the hollow of the throat, so the chin, the jaw and everything above lie outside the frame: no chin, jaw, lips, nose, eye or eyebrow anywhere in the frame (the first take showed the underside of her chin at the top edge; never again).
FIDELITY: the necklace: a 4 mm wide chain of open elongated paperclip links about 4 x 11 mm in polished 18k gold tone; one thick round spring-gate sailor ring about 22 mm across with a 14 mm opening, a small push-pin nub and a ribbed gate collar; one short straight bar about 15 mm long set with one row of about nine tiny clear stones, on a jump ring. The toggle is turned to the front. It must stay a sailor ring with a straight bar 0.6 to 0.7 times the ring, never a plain donut ring, a lobster clasp, or a curved or multi-row pave bar; no pendant; do not redesign or add anything.
CLASP POSE: the clasp is posed exactly as in reference 2: the bar lies across the upper left of the ring with its row of tiny stones facing the camera, on its jump ring, the ring hangs below it, and the spring gate with its small push-pin nub and ribbed collar sits at the right. Reference 2 is a much closer view than this picture: copy its construction and pose, never its framing or its size.
METAL: every link, the sailor ring, the gate, the bar, the jump ring and the last link are the same polished warm-neutral 18k gold tone, one tone only; never silver tone, white metal, rose tone, orange or brassy (an earlier take turned the bar's jump ring and the link beside it silver tone; never again).
SCALE, true size, the most important instruction: the necklace is fine against the body (the first take drew it about one and a half times too big; never again). The sailor ring is about 22 mm across, a little wider than a fingertip and a little larger than a 20 mm coin. The 50 cm chain lies along the collarbones and dips to the clasp, which rests flat on the skin of the upper breastbone about three ring-widths below the hollow of the throat, with a soft, true contact shadow. Her neck is about five ring-widths wide (about 11 cm), never three or four; the ring is narrower than the hollow between the two collarbone heads; the ring is about as wide as two paperclip links laid end to end; each side shows about twelve paperclip links between the side of the neck and the clasp, never eight or nine; her four fingers side by side are wider than three rings. Field of view about 15 cm wide.
HER: warm brown skin with soft natural creases at the neck and a few faint freckles, dignified and unretouched, never aged for effect; a rani-pink silk saree blouse with a plain round neckline with no zari, border or trim, its edge crossing the frame about one finger-width below the ring, at about 52% of the height; the pallu over her left shoulder (the frame's right).
PLACEMENT: the ring's centre at about 42% of the frame's height and about 45% of its width, a little above the middle of the frame; nothing of the necklace below 50%.
CLEAN SPACE ROUND THE CLASP: keep a calm, evenly lit area about 6.5 cm across centred on the clasp, the clasp sharp and fully visible: inside that area only the clasp, the chain and the skin it rests on; no fingers, glasses, temple arms, hair or fabric cross it, and nothing is in front of the clasp.
HER GLASSES: her own left hand (soft creases, short bare nails, no rings, no bangles, no watch, the wrist under the pallu) enters from the right edge and holds her folded reading glasses beside the clasp, never in front of it: half-moon reading glasses, flat-topped D-shaped lenses with the straight edge on top and the curve below, thin dark tortoiseshell rims, a thin bridge, both temple arms folded; she pinches one folded temple arm between thumb and fingers. The glasses sit to the right of the clasp at about its height, their nearest edge about 2 cm right of the clean area, and may run off the right edge; her fingers only in the right fifth of the frame, between 40% and 62% of the height. Never round, oval, panto, cat-eye or full-height lenses (an earlier take had a full-rim round lens). The glass is perfectly clear and untinted, with no reflection, glare or white sheen; through it only pink silk and skin, never the clasp, never a face or eyes.
